system:
Resolve reference/request licences for each visual attribute. Return only governs and reasons matching the supplied JSON contract. Interpret the complete request semantically, without keyword lists. The separate medium_decision already settles rendering-medium permission and taxonomy: the medium owner is pinned by the schema. Host code computes the style phrase, transformation phrase/target, discrepancy and note from the accepted medium decision. Do not return those host-owned fields.
With no visual reference, every visual attribute is request-governed. Otherwise the reference governs every attribute the user has not actually specified. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Independent reference_readings are real supplied readings even when this analysis attaches no conditioning media.
Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. For a non-frame content reference, sheet panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. For actual_frame sources, the entire supplied image is the target frame at its anchored instant: preserve those pixels, including their complete layout and source background. Never authorize sheet cleanup on an actual frame merely because it is a sheet. An observed pose is licensed only for an actual frame anchor, never as an identity attribute. Keep rendering restyling independent of retention relationship: changing a medium does not itself select attribute_transfer.
Target identities are already resolved by identity_requirements. Those are TARGET descriptors and properties after explicit caller requirements; original observed_subjects remain the SOURCE. Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. Resolve only the remaining attribute owners and their reasons.

brief.intent: the woman in the technical jacket rides the dragon into an epic battleground, cinematic hollywood scene with dramatic expressions and camera movements

cards.summary: A multi-panel character reference sheet for a solitary adult figure in an all-black tactical outfit, with a rainy nighttime rooftop hero panel above neutral full-body turnaround views and close-up details.

subjects.descriptor: Adult person with a shaved-side undercut and small topknot, the single character shown across the reference panels.
attributes: Short dark hair shaved close at the sides, gathered into a small topknot or braid at the crown
Black high-collared tactical jacket with zipper and strap or buckle details
Visible dirt or grime on the hands
pose: Hero panel: standing centered on the wet walkway, arms at sides, head turned to the viewer's right
Front panel: standing upright, facing the camera, arms at sides
Side profile panel: standing upright, facing the viewer's left
Back panel: standing upright, facing away from the camera
Face close-up: neutral expression, looking toward the camera

cards.environment: The hero panel is a wet urban rooftop or elevated walkway at night with metal railings and out-of-focus city lights; the reference panels use a plain dark studio backdrop.
cards.lighting: Low-key cinematic lighting: the hero panel has a bright overhead flare, warm practical lights, rain, and reflective wet ground; the studio panels use dim, soft directional light against a dark background.
cards.framing: Composite reference sheet: a wide low-angle full-body hero panel at top, a row of three full-body turnaround panels, and four close-up detail panels, each with a label beneath it.
cards.style: Cinematic, photorealistic character concept and reference sheet with dark tactical styling.

cards.summary: Dark fantasy dragon character reference sheet on a black background. A large hero panel shows a black, horned, bat-winged dragon in a volcanic landscape, with six labeled turnaround and detail panels below.

subjects.descriptor: Massive black dragon with long swept-back horns, spiked dorsal ridge, large bat-like wings, long tail, and pale claws.
attributes: spikes along the head, neck, back, and tail
large leathery bat-like wings with visible wing fingers
large clawed feet with pale claws
pose: Hero panel: standing on all fours with head lowered and wings partially extended
FRONT panel: facing viewer with wings spread
SIDE PROFILE panel: standing in profile with wings partly spread
REAR panel: viewed from behind with wings spread

cards.environment: Hero panel: dark volcanic terrain with jagged rock spires, smoky air, reflective wet ground, and glowing orange embers. Turnaround and detail panels use a plain dark backdrop.
cards.lighting: Low-key dramatic lighting with cool grey-blue highlights on the scales, warm orange ember glow in the background, and deep shadows.
cards.framing: Composite reference sheet: a wide hero panel across the top and six smaller panels in two rows below, showing front, side profile, rear, head close, wing membrane, claw and foot, and scale detail views.
cards.style: Dark fantasy creature concept art; photorealistic 3D-rendered character reference sheet.
cards.characterisation: A colossal, menacing black dragon with long horns, armored scales, a spiked dorsal ridge, and expansive bat-like wings.

rendering_permission.reasoning: The request describes scene action and appends a descriptive style phrase (“cinematic hollywood scene with dramatic expressions and camera movements”) rather than issuing a grammatical rendering operation or complete target-rendition directive. No explicit authorization to depart from the attached visual reference’s rendering is present.

medium_decision.retained_style: Cinematic, photorealistic with dark tactical styling
medium_decision.requested_style: hollywood scene with dramatic expressions and camera movements
medium_decision.reasoning: The host-owned rendering_permission is preserve, so no departure from the attached references is authorized. The first observed reference is a content reference sheet; its retained_style keeps the actual cinematic/photorealistic/dark tactical visual traits while removing reference-sheet packaging. Neither the reference phrase nor the request specifies a coarse rendering family, so both medium fields remain empty. The requested style phrase is retained, with cinematic classified as a compatible treatment.
